source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: Why is it useful that tapping a raised hand also shows the photos and names of neighboring seats, not just the student whose hand is raised?

options.text: It fills otherwise empty space on the instructor's screen
options.feedback: The notes present this as a working part of cold-calling, not as a way to use up room on the display.

options.text: It lets the instructor take attendance for the whole row at once
options.feedback: Attendance comes from check-in, which has already happened by the time anyone raises a hand, so nothing about tapping a hand records it.

options.text: It shows which nearby students have opted in to being cold-called
options.feedback: The 'OK to call on' highlight is already visible on the chart for everyone who opted in, so tapping a raised hand is not what reveals it.

options.text: It supports calling on that student or on someone sitting nearby
options.feedback: Seeing the neighbors alongside the raised hand leaves you a choice: take the hand that is up, or bring in someone close by who has not spoken yet.
